context.analysis:
## Overview
This system modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform by gradually migrating claim types from a 30-year-old mainframe to a cloud-native Azure environment. The hybrid architecture maintains business continuity and strict data consistency while operating alongside the legacy system of record.

## Key Elements
- End Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Operations Managers & Migration Auditors
- New Insurance Claims Platform (.NET Core, Azure Kubernetes Service)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL, DB2)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) & API Gateway
- Azure Service Bus with Dead-Letter Queues
- Identity Provider (on-premises Active Directory / Azure Entra ID)
- Centralized Audit Sink (Azure Application Insights, Azure Immutable Blob Storage)
- Infrastructure as Code (Bicep / Terraform)

## Relationships
- End Customers, Brokers, and Adjusters interact with the New Claims Platform via HTTPS/REST.
- New Claims Platform communicates with the Legacy Mainframe via asynchronous messaging over Azure Service Bus and an enterprise API Gateway.
- Hybrid services authenticate across boundaries using TLS 1.3 with mutual TLS (mTLS).
- Users authenticate via OpenID Connect (OIDC) / OAuth 2.0 integrated with Active Directory / Azure Entra ID.
- Claim state transitions log to Azure Immutable Blob Storage using WORM policies.

## Technology Stack
- **Azure Kubernetes Service (.NET Core):** Delivers scalable, cloud-native microservices for the new web application.
- **Azure Service Bus:** Provides asynchronous messaging and durable buffering to prevent message loss during batch windows.
- **Azure Key Vault & HSM:** Manages customer-managed keys for envelope encryption and hardware security module-backed mTLS certificates.
- **Azure Immutable Blob Storage:** Ensures tamper-proof, cryptographically immutable audit trails for compliance.
- **Bicep / Terraform:** Standardizes infrastructure as code to offset the team's limited cloud experience.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture decouples the modern Azure platform from legacy mainframe constraints using an Anti-Corruption Layer and asynchronous messaging. This ensures <2s UI performance, strict data consistency, and rapid one-day fallback capabilities without modifying the legacy system more than once per quarter.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system with a modern Azure-hosted platform while maintaining dual-system processing. It provides online claim submission, adjuster management, and incremental claim-type migration with rapid rollback capabilities.

## Key Elements
- End Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters & Migration Product Owners
- Web Frontend (SPA)
- Claims API Gateway
- Core Claims Service
- Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
- Integration & Transformation Worker
- Operational Observability & Dead-Letter Container
- Legacy COBOL/DB2 Mainframe
- Azure Key Vault & Active Directory (Entra ID)

## Relationships
- End Users to Web Frontend: HTTPS / REST / WebSockets
- Web Frontend to Claims API Gateway: HTTPS / REST
- Claims API Gateway to Core Claims Service: gRPC / internal HTTPS
- Core Claims Service to Mainframe ACL: Azure Event Hubs (Kafka)
- Mainframe ACL to Legacy Mainframe: IPsec VPN / Azure ExpressRoute (SFTP, MQ, Batch)
- Services to Azure Key Vault: Managed Identities (HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts the Web Frontend SPA for low operational overhead
- Azure API Management: Acts as the Claims API Gateway enforcing AD authentication
- Azure Container Apps: Runs containerized microservices due to team's cloud experience
- Azure Event Hubs (Kafka): Powers the Mainframe ACL for asynchronous decoupling
- Azure Key Vault: Secures Customer-Managed Keys and service credentials

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes using an asynchronous event-driven anti-corruption layer, protecting business continuity. Utilizing managed serverless Azure services minimizes complexity for a team with limited cloud experience while guaranteeing strict consistency, performance, and rollback requirements.

Web Frontend (SPA).analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a modern hybrid insurance claims platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe while maintaining continuous operations. The core purpose is to enable online claim submissions, adjuster workflows, and granular claim-type migrations without business disruption.]

## Key Elements
- End Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Migration Product Owners
- Web Frontend (SPA) (Azure Static Web Apps, React)
- Claims API Gateway (Azure API Management)
- Core Claims Service (Azure Container Apps)
- Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) (Azure Event Hubs / Kafka)
- Integration & Transformation Worker (Azure Container Apps)
- Operational Observability & Dead-Letter Container (Azure Container Apps, Azure Monitor)

## Relationships
- End Customers & Brokers -> Web Frontend (SPA): Submit and manage claims [HTTPS / REST / WebSockets]
- Claims Adjusters -> Web Frontend (SPA): Manage claims and adjusters [HTTPS / REST / WebSockets]
- Migration Product Owners -> Web Frontend (SPA): Monitor migration and rollbacks [HTTPS / REST / WebSockets]
- Web Frontend (SPA) -> Claims API Gateway: Sends API requests [HTTPS / REST]
- Claims API Gateway -> Core Claims Service: Routes service requests [HTTPS / gRPC]
- Core Claims Service -> Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Publishes domain events [AMQP / Kafka Protocol]
- Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) -> Legacy Mainframe: Synchronizes state [DB2 Direct / Batch / SNA]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts the React SPA with global CDN distribution to suit the team's limited cloud experience.
- React with MSAL.react: Implements OIDC/OAuth2 authentication via Authorization Code Flow with PKCE for Azure AD integration.
- TanStack Query: Provides local state caching to meet sub-2s performance requirements despite slow mainframe responses.
- IndexedDB with Web Crypto API (AES-GCM): Secures offline claim drafts locally on the client.
- Azure Application Insights: Tracks client-side performance and telemetry with automated PII scrubbing.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe interactions while modernizing front-end and integration layers incrementally. It satisfies strict operational constraints, ensures zero-loss migration consistency, and accommodates the team's limited cloud experience through managed Azure services.]

Claims API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern Azure-based architecture. Its core purpose is to enable online claim submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining seamless data consistency and zero downtime during the multi-year migration.

## Key Elements
- Claims API Gateway: Azure API Management (APIM)
- JWT Validation Policy Component: Validates tokens against Azure AD / Entra ID
- Rate Limiting & Throttling Component: APIM Policy enforcing persona-based quotas
- Claims-Based Authorization Policy Component: Enforces RBAC separation
- mTLS & Secure Connector Component: Manages certificate-based outbound trust
- Distributed Tracing Injector Component: Injects OpenTelemetry correlation headers
- Health Probing & Automated Failover Component: APIM backend probes and circuit breaker
- API Security Gateway Policies: OWASP Top 10 payload validation and sanitization
- Upstream Systems: Core Claims Service (Azure Container Apps) and Mainframe ACL (Azure Event Hubs)

## Relationships
- Web Frontend (SPA) -> Claims API Gateway: Sends API requests via [HTTPS / REST]
- Claims API Gateway -> Core Claims Service: Routes authenticated requests via [gRPC / internal HTTPS with mTLS]
- Claims API Gateway -> Mainframe ACL: Forwards fallback requests via [HTTPS with mTLS]
- Claims API Gateway -> Azure AD / Entra ID: Validates tokens via [OAuth2 / OpenID Connect]
- Claims API Gateway -> Azure App Configuration: Evaluates cached feature flags via [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure API Management (APIM): Core gateway container for centralized routing and security policies
- Azure AD / Entra ID: Identity provider for Single Sign-On and JWT validation
- Azure App Configuration: Backs dynamic feature flags for claim type routing and 1-day fallback
- OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing standard for cross-boundary observability
- Bicep: Infrastructure-as-Code for reproducible deployments and automated config rollbacks
- gRPC / HTTPS: Secure protocols for high-performance service-to-service and hybrid communication

## Rationale
This architecture uses an API Gateway pattern to abstract the hybrid migration complexity, ensuring the UI remains decoupled from backend shifts between the mainframe and Azure. Persona-based routing, automated failovers, and rigorous Infrastructure-as-Code enforce the strict 1-day rollback and sub-2-second performance requirements while mitigating the team's low cloud experience.

Core Claims Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Core Claims Service gradually modernizes a legacy insurance platform using a hybrid cloud architecture. It handles online submissions, adjuster workflows, and incremental claim type migrations while maintaining zero data loss.

## Key Elements
- Claim Orchestrator Component (Java / Spring Boot)
- Claim Domain Model Component (Java / DDD)
- ACL Publisher Component (Apache Kafka Client)
- Validation & Policy Engine Component (Spring Validation / Drools)
- SLA & Metrics Telemetry Component (Micrometer / OpenTelemetry)

## Relationships
- Core Claims Service -> Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer: Publishes asynchronous events [Apache Kafka / Azure Event Hubs]
- Core Claims Service -> Azure Key Vault & Active Directory: Retrieves secrets and validates tokens [Managed Identities / OAuth2 / HTTPS]
- Internal Components -> Internal Components: Executes direct in-process method calls [In-Memory]

## Technology Stack
- Java / Spring Boot: Chosen for robust enterprise ecosystem and team familiarity
- Azure Container Apps: Provides managed container orchestration with low operational overhead
- Spring Security & OAuth2: Enforces zero-trust token validation and RBAC/ABAC
- Micrometer & OpenTelemetry: Captures distributed traces and business metrics without leaking PII

## Rationale
This component-based architecture isolates modern business logic from rigid legacy constraints, enabling a one-day rollback per claim type. It mitigates the team's low cloud experience through managed Azure services and automated scaling.

Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL).analysis:
## Overview
[The Insurance Claims Platform modernizes a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system by gradually migrating claim types while maintaining continuous operations. It bridges the hybrid boundary using an enterprise-grade Anti-Corruption Layer with robust event streaming and circuit breaking.]

## Key Elements
*   [Core Claims Service (Azure Container Apps)]
*   [Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Event Hubs / Kafka)]
*   [Ingress Event Router (Kafka Connect / Azure Functions)]
*   [Schema & State Registry (Confluent Schema Registry)]
*   [Protocol Adapter (Apache Camel)]
*   [Legacy COBOL/DB2 Mainframe]
*   [Operational Observability & Dead-Letter Container]

## Relationships
*   [Core Claims Service -> Ingress Event Router: Publishes JSON CloudEvents via Azure Event Hubs]
*   [Ingress Event Router -> Schema & State Registry: Validates payloads via Confluent Schema Registry]
*   [Schema & State Registry -> Protocol Adapter: Dispatches validated transformation payloads]
*   [Protocol Adapter -> Legacy COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Transmits data via IBM MQ and SFTP over Azure ExpressRoute with mTLS and envelope encryption]
*   [Protocol Adapter -> Operational Observability & Dead-Letter Container: Routes poison pills to DLQ with automated PII masking]

## Technology Stack
*   [Azure Event Hubs (Kafka): Asynchronously decouples modern platform from legacy mainframe]
*   [Kafka Connect: Minimizes custom integration code for team with low cloud experience]
*   [Confluent Schema Registry: Enforces data contracts to limit mainframe changes to max one per quarter]
*   [Apache Camel: Provides enterprise integration patterns, circuit breaking, and retry logic]
*   [Azure Key Vault: Manages legacy service credentials dynamically via managed identities]

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates rigid mainframe legacy dependencies using bounded event-driven patterns and strict schema contracts. It guarantees zero claim loss, supports rapid daily rollbacks, and respects strict batch windows while upskilling a low-experience cloud team through managed services.]

Integration & Transformation Worker.analysis:
## Overview
Modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurer's legacy mainframe claims platform through a hybrid cloud architecture. Enables incremental claim type migration while ensuring zero data loss and maintaining legacy system operations.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: End Customers & Brokers, Claims Adjusters, Operations Managers & Migration Auditors
- **External Systems**: Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2), Identity Provider (Active Directory / Entra ID), Centralized Audit Sink
- **Containers**: Web Frontend (SPA), Claims API Gateway, Core Claims Service, Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL), Integration & Transformation Worker, Operational Observability & Dead-Letter Container
- **Worker Components**: Kafka Event Consumer, Schema & Policy Mapper, Idempotency & State Manager, Mainframe Protocol Dispatcher, Reconciliation & Audit Publisher

## Relationships
- **Kafka Event Consumer** reads from **Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer** via Apache Kafka / AMQP (SASL/SCRAM or mTLS)
- **Schema & Policy Mapper** queries **Idempotency & State Manager** via TLS-encrypted TCP (port 6380)
- **Schema & Policy Mapper** sends payloads to **Mainframe Protocol Dispatcher** via gRPC/HTTPS
- **Schema & Policy Mapper** emits telemetry to **Reconciliation & Audit Publisher** via OpenTelemetry SDK
- **Reconciliation & Audit Publisher** exports metrics to **Operational Observability & Dead-Letter Container** via HTTPS
- **Integration & Transformation Worker** retrieves secrets from **Azure Key Vault** via Managed Identities (HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
- **Azure Static Web Apps & React**: Powers the modern Web Frontend SPA for adjuster efficiency
- **Azure Container Apps**: Hosts scalable microservices and workers with KEDA-based scaling
- **Azure Event Hubs (Kafka)**: Bridges legacy and modern messaging via Apache Kafka protocol
- **Azure Cache for Redis**: Provides high-performance state storage for idempotency and duplicate prevention
- **Polly**: Implements circuit breaking for robust mainframe integration protection
- **OpenTelemetry & Azure Monitor**: Delivers distributed tracing and reconciliation observability

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes behind an Anti-Corruption Layer while enabling gradual, low-risk claim migration. Idempotent processing and strict circuit breakers protect system consistency and legacy constraints during the 3-year transition.

Operational Observability & Dead-Letter.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurance mainframe by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud platform while ensuring zero data loss. The Operational Observability & Dead-Letter Container monitors system health and manages failed message delivery.]

## Key Elements
- Dead-Letter Consumer Component (.NET 8 Worker)
- Re-drive Engine Component (.NET 8 Minimal API)
- Metrics & Tracing Collector (OpenTelemetry / Azure Monitor exporter)
- Operations API Component (.NET 8 Minimal API)
- Payload Normalization & Enrichment Component (.NET 8)

## Relationships
- Dead-Letter Consumer Component consumes failed messages from Azure Service Bus / Event Hubs DLQs via AMQP.
- Operations API Component exposes secure HTTPS endpoints for the Claims API Gateway and Operations Managers.
- Payload Normalization & Enrichment Component stores enriched payloads in Azure Blob Storage with HTTPS.
- Metrics & Tracing Collector exports telemetry to Azure Monitor over HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
- .NET 8 on Azure Container Apps for lightweight, fast component isolation.
- Azure Blob Storage with structured JSON indexing for searchable dead-letter payloads.
- OpenTelemetry and Azure Monitor for centralized system health and distributed tracing.
- Azure Active Directory and TLS 1.3 for secure authentication and transport encryption.

## Rationale
[This architecture provides strict resilience and idempotency controls to satisfy zero-loss migration mandates (R-04) despite limited cloud team experience. It bridges deep technical errors with business-context triage to ensure operational continuity.]
